newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Court rules in favour of Vietnam bank over LC row.
newsitem.headline: Court rules in favour of Vietnam bank over LC row.

text.p: A Vietnamese state-owned bank whose assets in seven Singapore banks were frozen in June in a row over payment on a Letter of Credit (LC) said on Thursday it had succeeded in having the judgement set aside.

A statement issued by the Industrial and Commercial Bank of Vietnam (Vietincombank) said the bank had argued successfully in a Singapore court against an injunction obtained by Mees Pierson N.V. (Singapore branch) ordering its local nostro accounts frozen.

The statement said the court had accepted arguments, including that Mees Pierson had not been instructed or authorised to act as confirming bank in the LC deal, and that a writ of summons issued against Vietincombank's Binh Thuan branch had been irregular under Vietnamese law.
Mees Pierson in Singapore had no immediate comment on the statement.
The dispute between the two companies first came to court in June and centred around a letter of credit involving some $500,000 and a shipment of flour, which never arrived.
News of the row surfaced last week, following months of troubles in the communist country's domestic banking system linked to letter of credit and other debt repayments.
Bankers in Hanoi said the development was a further blow to an industry already reeling from problems associated with scandal surrounding loans made to two major conglomerates, Minh Phung and Epco.

Vietincombank's statement said Mees Pierson had been ordered to pay costs, and added that the firm had since withdrawn orders freezing the nostro accounts of Vietincombank in seven banks in Singapore.
